source_text.docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml:
id: ISS-0439
title: "Design exploration: should Letflow offer typed business-object templates (1C-style Directory/Document/Register/Report) over the generic entity subsystem? Deliberately DEFERRED pending real usage"
acceptance_criteria:
  - "The decision to defer, and the three reasons for it, are recorded somewhere a future reader will find before re-proposing the idea -- a decision record under docs/migration/decisions/ is the expected home"
  - "The review triggers are stated explicitly (a concrete domain; observed duplication of Directory/Register-shaped structures across tenants; an ERP-adjacent market decision) so the deferral is reviewable rather than permanent"
  - "The mapping of the 1C taxonomy onto Letflow's EXISTING machinery is stated -- specifically which of Directory/Document/Register/Report is already served by the event log, by projections, by Letflow.EventStore.Registry's typed payload schemas, and by the repository's artifact versioning -- so a future design starts from what exists rather than from a blank page"
  - "The dependency on the generic entity subsystem (queue task 438) is stated: no typed-template design proceeds until that subsystem's scope status is settled"
  - "No requirements are created, no schema is defined, and no code is written by this issue"
  - "If the eventual conclusion is that Letflow should NOT adopt the taxonomy at all, that verdict is recorded with its reasoning rather than the issue being closed silently"

task.description:
ISS-0439 is a DESIGN-EXPLORATION-ONLY issue (read docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml in full for the complete filing, including the user's original three-reasons-for-deferral text and the 'what would change this' triggers -- do not re-derive that reasoning from scratch, restate/ground it). It builds nothing: no requirements, no schema, no implementation code. Your job is to produce TWO artefacts, both prose/design-exploration only:

1. A design-exploration artefact under lib/letflow/design/ (suggested filename: iss0439-1c-taxonomy-mapping.md) that maps the 1C taxonomy (Directory/Document/Register/Report) onto Letflow's EXISTING machinery. For each of the four 1C concepts, state concretely and with real module/file citations (read the actual current code, not just ISS-0439's own claims -- its filing was written 2026-09-02 and things may have shifted):
   - Directories: is there an existing Letflow mechanism serving 'relatively constant reference data'? Consider the entity subsystem's scoping decision (lib/letflow/design/iss0438-entity-subsystem-scoping.md) -- entity definitions/records are the closest current analogue, even though ISS-0438's own subsystem is not yet built (7 requirements REQ-225..REQ-231 registered, none done as of this run -- verify their current status in docs/requirements.yaml rather than trusting this sentence).
   - Documents: does the append-only event log genuinely serve as a 'document journal' recording intent/operations? Read lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex to confirm what it actually does and does not provide (schema versioning, not posting semantics).
   - Registers: do instance_projections or similar projection mechanisms genuinely serve as 'registers' recording consequences? Find and read the actual projection module(s) -- grep for 'projection' under lib/letflow/ to locate them; do not assume iss0438's scoping doc's characterization is complete.
   - Reports: is there an existing query/presentation layer over projections? Note: the entity subsystem's query/ subsystem (QRY-01..05, described in the iss0438 scoping doc's slice 6) is itself unbuilt -- state plainly whether ANY reporting layer exists today over ANY projection, or whether this is entirely aspirational.
   For each of the four, be explicit about what is ALREADY THERE (genuine reuse) versus what would be GENUINELY NEW (a real gap, not mere renaming). Do not restate ISS-0439's filed claims uncritically -- verify each against the current codebase and note any correction if the 2026-09-02 filing's characterization turns out to be inaccurate or stale as of this run (2026-09-04).
   State plainly Letflow.EventStore.Registry's role (typed payload schema versioning) and Letflow.Repository's role (artifact/content versioning) explicitly, per this issue's own AC3.
   State the ISS-0438 dependency explicitly (AC4): no typed-template design should proceed while the generic entity subsystem's own requirements (REQ-225..REQ-231) are still unimplemented -- name their current docs/requirements.yaml status.

2. A decision record at docs/migration/decisions/0019-<slug>.md (0019 is the next free number as of this dispatch -- re-verify by listing docs/migration/decisions/ yourself before writing, in case a concurrent run has claimed it) that:
   - States the deferral decision and its three reasons VERBATIM from the user's original framing (quoted in docs/issues/ISS-0439.yaml's description field) -- do not paraphrase away the reasoning, this is the artefact a future reader must find before re-proposing the idea.
   - States the three review triggers explicitly (concrete tenant/domain; observed cross-tenant duplication of Directory/Register-shaped structures; an ERP-adjacent market decision) so the deferral reads as reviewable, not permanent.
   - States the ISS-0438 dependency (no typed-template design proceeds until the generic entity subsystem's scope status -- now IN SCOPE, S6, REQ-225..REQ-231 -- is itself built, not merely scoped).
   - Cross-references artefact #1 (the taxonomy mapping) so a reader lands on the concrete grounding, not just the narrative decision.
   - Follow this project's existing decision-record format/style -- read 2-3 existing records under docs/migration/decisions/ (e.g. 0017 and 0018, the two most recent) to match structure and tone before writing.

Both artefacts are prose analysis and narrative decision text ONLY. No Elixir code, no @spec, no Ecto schema field lists, no JSON schema literals -- if you find yourself writing a code block, stop; describe the shape in prose instead, exactly as CODE-DESIGNER did for the iss0438 scoping artefact (which contains zero code blocks and was PASSed on exactly that basis).

Do not create any docs/requirements.yaml entries. Do not touch lib/letflow/ (implementation code) or priv/repo/migrations/. Do not touch lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex or any other existing module -- read-only for grounding.
acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/design/iss0439-*.md exists and maps all four of Directory/Document/Register/Report onto specifically-named existing Letflow modules/mechanisms (or explicitly states 'no existing mechanism' where genuinely true), each claim grounded in a module this run actually read, not assumed from ISS-0439's own filing text
The artefact explicitly separates 'already exists, would be reuse' from 'genuinely new, would need building' for each of the four taxonomy concepts

docs/migration/decisions/0019-*.md exists, states the deferral decision, the three reasons (in the user's own weighting/framing, quoted from ISS-0439.yaml, not diluted), and the three review triggers verbatim in substance

The decision record states the ISS-0438/REQ-225..231 dependency explicitly, including their CURRENT status (verified against docs/requirements.yaml at time of writing, not the 2026-09-02 filing's characterization)
Neither artefact contains a fenced code block of Elixir, Ecto schema, or JSON schema -- prose and structured lists only
Neither artefact creates, edits, or references creating any docs/requirements.yaml entry

If your own analysis concludes the taxonomy should NOT be adopted at all (a legitimate possible outcome per this issue's own AC6), state that verdict and its reasoning explicitly in the decision record rather than defaulting to a neutral 'still deferred' framing that avoids taking a position

result.summary: Produced two prose-only artefacts for ISS-0439 (deliberately deferred design exploration): (1) lib/letflow/design/iss0439-1c-taxonomy-mapping.md maps Directory/Document/Register/Report onto Letflow's actual code, read this session -- event log + Letflow.EventStore.Registry (typed payload schema versioning, real reuse for Document's journal half) + Letflow.EventStore.InstanceProjection (instance_projections, real reuse for Register's rebuildable-projection pattern) + Letflow.Repository/ArtifactKind (definition storage, not yet extended with :entity). Directory and Report have no existing mechanism at all -- stated plainly, not hedged. Document's posting-step and Register's generic ledger/aggregation semantics are stated as genuine gaps. Verdict given (not neutral): sequencing (build generic substrate, watch usage) is the right call, not outright rejection. (2) docs/migration/decisions/0019-defer-1c-typed-templates.md records the deferral with the three reasons quoted verbatim from ISS-0439.yaml, the three review triggers, and the REQ-225..231 dependency -- re-verified directly against docs/requirements.yaml this session: all seven still status: pending, none done. 0019 re-confirmed as next free decision-record number by directory listing before writing. Neither artefact contains a fenced code block (grep verified) or touches docs/requirements.yaml or lib/letflow/ implementation.
